qp_dispositions.rationale: Direct recognition of whether entries are real is definition-level classification; no distinct multi-step JEE reasoning mechanism is present in the source possibility.

A parameterized matrix can require simultaneous constraints from multiple entries; extracting and solving all reality conditions is a reusable parameter-constraint mechanism. Candidate only; academic approval and question-level validation remain pending.
For real matrices, entrywise addition and subtraction preserve real entries directly. This is a basic closure fact and does not justify a separate archetype from the stated possibility.

Products and integer powers of real matrices remain real by entrywise closure under multiplication and addition. The stated possibility is a direct closure check without a distinct reasoning mechanism.

Determining when a linear combination of real matrices remains real can require constraints on complex scalar coefficients and matrix linear independence; this differs from imposing reality conditions on matrix entries themselves. Candidate only; validate against representative JEE questions before approval.
Transpose only reorders the entries of a real matrix, so realness is preserved directly. This is a definition-level closure property rather than a distinct JEE archetype.

For a real matrix, entrywise conjugation leaves every entry unchanged and the conjugate transpose reduces to the transpose. The stated possibility is direct property recognition without an independent inference mechanism.

The inverse of an invertible real matrix is real, as follows from standard inverse/determinant or linear-system properties. The source possibility states a direct closure theorem and does not by itself define a distinct JEE archetype.

Polynomial and defined rational expressions with real coefficients preserve real entries under the stated operations. This is a direct closure/property check; a richer task would require a separately specified mechanism.
Trace, determinant, minors and cofactors of a real matrix are real by their definitions as sums and products of real entries. This is direct property application, not a distinct archetype.

The inclusion chain for integer-, rational-, real- and complex-entry matrices follows entrywise from the corresponding scalar number sets. This is direct hierarchy recognition and does not justify a separate JEE archetype.

An m×n real matrix has mn independently selectable real entries by definition. Counting these parameters is a direct dimension/counting fact; a distinct linear-algebra constraint problem would need a separately specified source possibility.
Translating R^{m×n} or M_{m×n}(R) is notation recognition for the set of real matrices of fixed order. It is prerequisite knowledge rather than a distinct assessment mechanism.
Classifying a matrix as real or complex from its entries is direct definition-level recognition. It is retained as foundation content and is not a separate JEE archetype.
Taking the complex conjugate entrywise is a direct operation. Without additional constraints or a multi-step inference, the source possibility does not justify a distinct JEE archetype.
Computing a conjugate transpose is a direct entrywise conjugation-and-transposition procedure. It is prerequisite matrix manipulation and does not by itself justify a distinct archetype.
Hermitian verification compares the matrix with its conjugate transpose; this is a direct structural check and is retained as foundation material.
Skew-Hermitian verification compares the conjugate transpose with the negative matrix. It is the sign counterpart of Hermitian verification, not a separate reasoning archetype.

Unitary verification requires checking the conjugate-transpose product against the identity matrix. This is a distinct matrix-condition verification mechanism and is retained as a JEE Main candidate, pending academic review.

Solving parameter conditions for Hermitian, skew-Hermitian or unitary structure requires translating a matrix identity into coupled real/imaginary constraints. This is a distinct parameter-constraint mechanism and remains a JEE Main candidate pending academic review.
The canonical decomposition into Hermitian and skew-Hermitian components is a reusable construction with a verifiable uniqueness structure; retained as a JEE Main candidate pending academic review.
Scalar multiplication effects on Hermitian/skew-Hermitian type follow directly from conjugate-transpose identities and real/imaginary scalar conditions; this is a concise property check.
Sum/difference type outcomes are direct closure checks and can be summarized by a small operation table; no independent multi-step mechanism is justified by the source possibility alone.

Products and inverses require applying adjoint identities, reversing factor order and respecting commutativity/invertibility conditions; this is a reusable multi-step matrix-structure mechanism, retained as a JEE Main candidate.
The adjoint identities are foundational transformation rules. Memorizing or directly applying the identities alone does not establish a separate archetype from product/adjoint reasoning.

Orthonormal rows/columns provide an equivalent characterization of unitarity already represented by the conjugate-transpose identity candidate. Retain as a variation/reference, not a duplicate archetype.
Diagonal and trace constraints are direct consequences of Hermitian/skew-Hermitian definitions and overlap with the parameter-constraint candidate. No separate mechanism is justified.
The real symmetric/skew-symmetric/orthogonal correspondences are direct special cases of the complex matrix classes; this is conceptual mapping rather than a distinct assessment mechanism.
Identifying a row matrix from its one-row order is a direct shape definition and remains foundation content.
Determining row-matrix order and indexing constraints is direct dimensional interpretation; no distinct JEE reasoning mechanism is justified by the source possibility.
Solving for a matrix to have exactly one row is a direct shape constraint on its order; it is a foundation-level classification task.
Constructing a one-row matrix from supplied entries or a pattern is direct representation and does not establish a distinct JEE reasoning mechanism.
A row matrix is also square or a column matrix only in the 1×1 case; this is a direct order-definition check.
Equality with a given row matrix requires matching order and corresponding entries, which is a direct matrix-equality prerequisite.
Addition and scalar multiplication preserve the one-row shape when orders match; this is a direct closure property.
Recognizing a one-column order is a direct definition check and remains foundation content.
Constructing a column matrix from entries or a rule is direct representation, not a distinct reasoning mechanism.
Equality of column matrices follows by matching order and corresponding entries; this is a basic matrix-equality check.
The transpose of a column matrix is a row matrix of the corresponding order; this is a direct shape transformation.
Checking whether an operation is defined from operand dimensions is prerequisite compatibility reasoning and does not establish a distinct JEE archetype here.
Determining the order/type of a defined expression from column-matrix dimensions is routine dimension arithmetic and remains foundation content.
Parameter conditions for one-column order reduce directly to the row-count/column-count definition; no distinct JEE reasoning mechanism is established.
A column matrix is square only when it is 1×1; this is a direct order-definition check.
Extracting a specified column from a matrix is direct representation and indexing.
The number of elements equals the row count for an n×1 matrix; this is direct order interpretation.
Rectangularity is a direct comparison of row and column counts; it is a definition-level classification.
Distinguishing row, column and general rectangular matrices follows directly from order dimensions and is foundation-level.
Determining admissible matrix orders from row/column constraints is routine integer/dimension reasoning and does not establish a distinct JEE mechanism here.
Addition/subtraction compatibility requires equal orders and the resulting order is unchanged; this is a basic dimension check.
Product compatibility and resulting order follow the standard inner-dimension rule; the source possibility alone does not justify a separate archetype.
Testing self-operations involving a rectangular matrix and its transpose is primarily order-compatibility checking; the source possibility does not yet define a distinct mechanism.
Determining whether square-only constructs apply is a direct check of whether row and column counts match; retain as foundation content.
Transpose swaps row and column counts and changes row/column type directly; this is a basic representation property.
Inferring whether a matrix is square or rectangular from several operation-definedness constraints can require solving coupled order conditions; retained as a JEE Main candidate.
Identity-matrix orders that preserve a rectangular matrix follow directly from compatible dimensions and are retained as foundation content.
Recognizing square shape and stating its order is a direct row-count/column-count definition check.

Parameter conditions for squareness reduce to equality of row and column counts; this is a simple order constraint and overlaps the existing dimension-inference mechanism without adding a distinct one.

Determining whether an expression is square from the orders of its operands is routine dimension tracking and overlaps the existing operation-definedness candidate unless a distinct multi-constraint task is specified.
Checking whether determinant, trace, inverse, eigenvalues or characteristic polynomial apply is a direct square-matrix prerequisite check.
Identifying principal or secondary diagonal entries is direct positional recognition within a square matrix.
Counting diagonal and off-diagonal positions follows directly from the n×n grid and standard position formulas; no distinct matrix-type reasoning mechanism is justified.
Closure of square matrices under standard operations is a direct property check and remains foundation content.
Inferring squareness from square-only constructs is a useful diagnostic, but it overlaps the existing operation-definedness/dimension-inference candidate and is not split into another archetype.
Determining total row/column dimensions from block-size constraints can require combining several independent block equations; retained as a distinct JEE Main candidate pending academic review.
Zero-matrix recognition by checking all entries is a direct definition-level task.
Requiring every entry of a parameterized matrix to vanish gives entrywise zero equations; this is direct parameter substitution/solving and remains foundation-level.
The zero matrix order must match the given matrix for addition/subtraction; this is direct dimension compatibility.
Using the zero matrix as additive identity is a direct algebraic simplification rule.
Products with a zero matrix produce a zero matrix of compatible order; this is a direct operation property.
The implication AB=O ⇒ A=O or B=O is false for matrices; constructing nonzero zero-divisor matrices or reasoning through nullspaces is a distinct reusable inference/counterexample mechanism.
Scalar-multiplication zero implications split directly on whether the scalar is zero; this is a short property check and remains foundation-level.
Transpose preserves the zero entries and swaps the matrix order; this is a direct transformation property.
The zero matrix satisfies several standard structural definitions by direct substitution; this is classification by definitions.
Determinant and trace of a zero square matrix follow directly from their definitions and are retained as foundation facts.
Integer powers require careful treatment of positive, zero and negative exponents, including square-matrix and invertibility conditions; this is a distinct boundary-condition assessment mechanism.
A nonempty square zero matrix is singular and therefore has no inverse; this is a direct standard property check.
The zero matrix of a fixed order is unique by entrywise equality; this is a direct definition/proof fact.
A−B=O iff A=B follows immediately by adding B to both sides or comparing entries; this is a foundational equality identity.
Diagonal-matrix recognition is a direct check that every off-diagonal entry is zero.
Imposing diagonality on a parameterized matrix requires simultaneous zero constraints on all off-diagonal entries; this is a reusable parameter-constraint mechanism and a JEE Main candidate.
For a diagonal matrix, determinant and nonsingularity reduce to the product/nonzero status of diagonal entries; this is a direct property check.
The inverse of an invertible diagonal matrix is obtained by reciprocating each nonzero diagonal entry; this is a direct standard formula.
Diagonal matrices are closed under compatible standard operations and commute under multiplication; these are direct algebraic properties.
Powers and polynomial expressions in a diagonal matrix can be evaluated entrywise on the diagonal, giving a reusable reduction of matrix expressions to scalar evaluations.
Left and right multiplication by a diagonal matrix scale rows and columns respectively; reasoning about the entry transformation is a distinct reusable mechanism.
Solving D²=D, D^k=I or D^m=O entrywise produces simultaneous scalar equations on diagonal entries; this is a reusable equation-constraint mechanism.

A diagonal matrix that commutes with every matrix must have equal diagonal entries, so it is scalar. Proving this universal property by testing off-diagonal matrix units is a distinct reasoning mechanism.
Recognizing a scalar matrix from its diagonal form is direct definition-level classification.
Distinguishing scalar, diagonal and identity matrices is direct comparison of definitions and remains foundation content.
Imposing the scalar-matrix form on a parameterized matrix requires all off-diagonal entries to vanish and all diagonal entries to agree; this is a reusable simultaneous-constraint mechanism.
Constructing a scalar matrix from a specified scalar and order is direct notation/definition application.
Equivalent characterizations of scalar matrices overlap the universal-commutativity mechanism already represented by the scalar-matrix candidate; no duplicate archetype is created.
Addition and multiplication of scalar matrices reduce to scalar arithmetic and preserve scalar-matrix form directly.
Multiplication by a scalar matrix gives uniform scaling and commutation; the universal-commutation reasoning is already represented by the existing candidate.
A scalar matrix is invertible exactly when its scalar is nonzero, with inverse the reciprocal scalar times identity; this is a direct property.
Integer powers of a scalar matrix reduce to scalar powers and direct invertibility conditions; this is a straightforward consequence of scalar-matrix form.
The adjugate of a scalar matrix follows a standard order-dependent formula; direct formula recall/application is retained as foundation content.
Determinant and trace reduce to λ^n and nλ respectively; these are direct standard formulas.
Rank, nullity and singularity reduce to the λ=0 versus λ≠0 case split; this is direct property classification.

A scalar matrix λI satisfies each listed structural property exactly when λ obeys a corresponding scalar equation; solving and consolidating these conditions is a reusable parameter-classification mechanism.
Recovering the scalar value from entries or stated conditions is direct parameter identification within λI and overlaps the scalar-property constraint candidate.
Counting admissible scalar matrices reduces to counting admissible scalar values under the stated entry restrictions; the source possibility does not establish a distinct reusable JEE mechanism.
Existence/uniqueness for constrained scalar matrices overlaps the existing scalar-parameter equation mechanism and is not split into another archetype.
A polynomial in λI reduces to p(λ)I by direct substitution; this is a standard evaluation rule.
Identity-matrix recognition is direct comparison with the diagonal ones and off-diagonal zeros.
Constructing I_n is direct notation and definition application.
Choosing compatible identity-matrix orders for left/right multiplication follows directly from dimensions; this remains foundation-level.
Simplification using the identity property is direct algebraic substitution.
For I_n, determinant, trace and rank are direct order-based formulas.
The identity matrix satisfies standard properties by direct definition; classification is a foundation check.
Existence and uniqueness of the identity matrix for a fixed order follow from the defining entry pattern and two-sided identity property; this is foundational algebra.
Determining left/right identity matrices for a particular rectangular matrix is direct order compatibility and identity action.

The source possibility does not specify the algebraic conditions. Different condition sets can imply different conclusions, so a safe disposition requires a concrete, source-faithful specification before an archetype can be assessed.
The identity matrix has eigenvalue 1 with multiplicity equal to its order; its spectral facts are direct standard properties.
Transpose, inverse and integer powers of an identity matrix return the identity of the compatible order; these are direct properties.
Upper-triangular recognition is a direct check that all entries below the main diagonal are zero.
Requiring all entries below the main diagonal of a parameterized matrix to vanish gives a simultaneous structural constraint system; retained as a JEE Main candidate.
The inclusion relationships among upper triangular, diagonal, scalar and identity matrices follow directly from their definitions.
Addition and scalar multiplication preserve upper-triangular form by direct entrywise closure.
Products, powers and polynomial expressions preserve upper-triangular form by the standard zero-pattern multiplication rule; this is a direct structural property.
If a matrix is both upper and lower triangular, all off-diagonal entries vanish and it is diagonal; transpose simply swaps the triangular direction.
An upper-triangular matrix is invertible exactly when every diagonal entry is nonzero, and its inverse remains upper triangular; this is a reusable structure-plus-invertibility mechanism.
A strictly upper-triangular n×n matrix is nilpotent with a finite power bound derived from the zero pattern; proving the bound by tracking index paths is a distinct reasoning mechanism.
The number of independent entries in an upper-triangular n×n matrix is a direct count of diagonal and above-diagonal positions.
The source does not specify which elementary row/column operations are in scope. Different operations preserve or destroy triangularity differently; an exact operation list is needed.
For upper-triangular factors, the diagonal of a product is the entrywise product of factor diagonals, and powers follow by repeated application; this is a reusable structural inference mechanism.
Lower-triangular recognition is a direct check that all entries above the main diagonal vanish.
Strict/unit lower-triangular classification follows directly from the zero pattern and diagonal entries.
Counting independent lower-triangular entries and forced zeros is a direct positional count.
Addition and scalar multiplication preserve lower-triangular form by direct entrywise closure.
The product of lower-triangular matrices remains lower triangular by the zero-pattern multiplication rule; this is a direct closure property.
Transpose converts lower-triangular form to upper-triangular form by swapping indices; this is a direct shape transformation.
A matrix that is both upper and lower triangular is diagonal; a symmetric lower-triangular matrix is likewise diagonal by entry symmetry. This is a direct structural implication.
Powers preserve lower-triangular form by repeated closure under multiplication; this is a direct property.

Diagonal entries of lower-triangular products/powers follow the same componentwise rule as upper-triangular matrices; it duplicates the existing archetype mechanism and is retained as a foundation variation.
Requiring a parameterized matrix to be lower triangular imposes simultaneous zero constraints on all entries above the main diagonal; this is a reusable parameter-constraint mechanism.
The inverse of a nonsingular lower-triangular matrix remains lower triangular; this mirrors the existing upper-triangular inverse mechanism and is not duplicated.
Invertibility is equivalent to nonzero diagonal entries, the same diagonal-product criterion already represented by the triangular inverse candidate.
Strictly lower-triangular nilpotency and its order bound mirror the existing strictly upper-triangular nilpotency mechanism; retain as a variation, not a duplicate.
Symmetric-matrix recognition is a direct comparison of the matrix with its transpose.
Symmetry imposes pairwise equality between corresponding transposed entries; solving these simultaneous parameter constraints is a reusable structural-constraint mechanism.
The number of independent entries is n diagonal entries plus one entry for each unordered off-diagonal pair; this is a direct count.
The symmetric component is (A+Aᵀ)/2, a direct formula that is included in the full decomposition mechanism.
Every square matrix decomposes as (A+Aᵀ)/2 plus (A−Aᵀ)/2; constructing and verifying both components is a reusable decomposition mechanism.
Uniqueness follows by adding/subtracting the symmetric and skew-symmetric parts; this is a direct consequence of the decomposition and is not a separate archetype.
Linear combinations of symmetric matrices with scalar coefficients remain symmetric by transpose linearity; this is a direct closure property.
A product AB is symmetric exactly when AB=BᵀAᵀ; for symmetric A and B this reduces to AB=BA. Identifying and applying the commutativity condition is a distinct reusable mechanism.
Powers and polynomial expressions in a symmetric matrix remain symmetric by transpose and power identities; this is a direct property.
The inverse of an invertible symmetric matrix is symmetric by the transpose-of-inverse identity; this is a direct property.
The adjugate of a symmetric matrix is symmetric by the transpose/cofactor identity; this is a direct property.
Expressions such as A+Aᵀ and A−Aᵀ have direct symmetric/skew-symmetric properties by transpose identities.
A congruence transform PᵀAP preserves symmetry whenever A is symmetric; proving this by transpose reversal is a distinct reusable structural-preservation mechanism.
An entry-wise matrix rule is symmetric when f(i,j)=f(j,i); this is a direct pairwise definition check and overlaps the existing symmetry-constraint mechanism.
A block-partitioned matrix is symmetric exactly when diagonal blocks are symmetric and opposite off-diagonal blocks are transposes; this is a distinct block-structure constraint mechanism.
A matrix that is both symmetric and triangular must be diagonal because transposed off-diagonal entries force both sides to zero.
A matrix that is both symmetric and skew-symmetric is zero over the real/complex fields; this is a direct consequence of Aᵀ=A and Aᵀ=−A.
The source does not specify the transpose relations or assumptions. A safe archetype cannot be defined until representative conditions are supplied.
The entry constraints and field are unspecified, so the count of admissible symmetric matrices is not determined by this possibility label alone.
Skew-symmetric classification is a direct check of Aᵀ=−A and the implied zero diagonal over the real/complex fields.
Skew-symmetry imposes paired negative-entry constraints and zero diagonal entries; solving parameter/missing-entry conditions is a distinct reusable structural-constraint mechanism.
The skew-symmetric component is (A−Aᵀ)/2 and is part of the full symmetric/skew-symmetric decomposition already represented by AR00024.
Zero diagonal entries and zero trace follow directly from Aᵀ=−A over the real/complex fields.
The general element-wise form follows by choosing one free value for each pair above/below the diagonal and negating the transposed entry; this is a direct representation fact.
The number of independent parameters is n(n−1)/2, one for each off-diagonal pair; this is a direct count.
Addition, subtraction, scalar multiplication, transpose and negation preserve skew-symmetry by direct transpose identities.

For a skew-symmetric K, (K^m)ᵀ=(−1)^mK^m, so powers alternate symmetric/skew-symmetric; polynomial expressions require separating even and odd powers. This is a reusable parity-based structure mechanism.
Transpose reversal and sign rules produce a classification table for products, commutators and anticommutators of symmetric/skew-symmetric matrices; this is a distinct multi-case algebraic mechanism.
Every odd-order skew-symmetric matrix is singular because det(A)=det(Aᵀ)=det(−A)=−det(A); even order permits but does not guarantee invertibility. This is a reusable parity/invertibility mechanism.
If an invertible matrix is skew-symmetric, its inverse is skew-symmetric by the transpose-of-inverse identity; this is a direct property.
A matrix both symmetric and skew-symmetric is zero over the real/complex fields; this duplicates the earlier foundation disposition.
The allowed discrete entry set and counting constraints are not specified, so the number of skew-symmetric matrices cannot be determined safely from this source possibility alone.
Orthogonality is checked directly by QᵀQ=I (equivalently QQᵀ=I for square matrices); basic recognition is retained as foundation content.
Orthogonality imposes coupled column/row norm and orthogonality equations on the parameters; solving these simultaneous constraints is a reusable JEE Main candidate mechanism.
Completing missing entries to form an orthogonal matrix requires constructing an orthonormal completion subject to existing row/column constraints, distinct from merely verifying a supplied matrix.
For an orthogonal matrix, Q^{-1}=Qᵀ is the defining inverse relation and is a direct property.
Orthogonal matrices have determinant ±1; the sign distinguishes orientation. Inferring the determinant restriction and classifying orientation is a distinct reusable invariant mechanism.
Products, transposes, inverses and integer powers preserve orthogonality by direct multiplication identities; this is a foundation-level group-property check.
The matrix identity and orthonormal-row/column characterizations are equivalent by direct row/column inner-product expansion.
Orthogonality gives unit column norms, zero cross-dot products, total squared-entry sum n and entrywise bounds; combining these constraints is a distinct reusable inference mechanism.
Special-family classification reduces orthogonality to conditions such as diagonal entries ±1 or orthogonal blocks; this is a reusable structural classification mechanism.
For a real scalar c and orthogonal Q, (cQ)ᵀ(cQ)=c²I, so orthogonality requires c=±1; for a general A, the condition reduces to c²AᵀA=I. This is a reusable scalar-constraint mechanism.
Row/column permutations and sign changes preserve orthonormality by permuting or negating orthonormal vectors; this is a direct invariance property.
Orthogonal matrices are necessarily square, full-rank and nonsingular because QᵀQ=I; this is a direct structural prerequisite check.
Orthogonal transformations preserve inner products and hence vector lengths and angles; applying this to vector constraints is a distinct metric-invariance mechanism.
Combining orthogonality with symmetry/skew-symmetry produces additional identities such as Q²=I or Q²=−I and field/order restrictions; this is a distinct combined-structure mechanism.

The independent degrees of freedom of an n×n real orthogonal matrix are n(n−1)/2, reflecting n(n+1)/2 independent orthogonality equations with dependencies; counting this constraint dimension is a distinct parameter-count mechanism.
Singularity is directly identified by determinant zero (for a square matrix); this is definition-level classification.
A parameterized matrix is singular exactly when its determinant vanishes; expanding and solving det(A(λ))=0 gives a reusable parameter-constraint mechanism.
Determinant multiplicativity and scalar/power rules allow singularity to be propagated or disproved through products, scalar factors and powers, with important converse distinctions.

Transpose, similarity and invertible elementary row/column operations preserve rank and hence singularity; distinguishing invariant operations from determinant scaling is a reusable transformation-invariance mechanism.
Determinant zero, non-invertibility, rank deficiency and row/column dependence are equivalent standard characterizations; direct recognition is foundation content.

The adjugate's structure depends on rank: for nonsingular A it is invertible; for rank n−1 it is nonzero of rank one; for rank at most n−2 it is zero. This is a distinct rank-sensitive inference mechanism.
Non-singularity recognition is a direct nonzero-determinant/invertibility check.
Parameter conditions for non-singularity reduce to det(A(λ))≠0 and complement the existing determinant-zero parameter mechanism; no duplicate archetype is created.
The equivalent characterizations of non-singularity are standard rank/determinant/inverse facts and remain foundation content.
Transpose, powers, nonzero scalar multiples and adjugates of nonsingular matrices have standard determinant/inverse consequences; this is a direct property set.
For square matrices of the same order, AB is nonsingular iff both A and B are nonsingular; proving both directions and testing converse implications is a reusable product-factor mechanism.
A is nonsingular exactly when Ax=b has a unique solution for every b; this links invertibility, existence and uniqueness in a reusable system-solving mechanism.
Elementary row/column operations are multiplication by invertible elementary matrices, so they preserve rank and nonsingularity while changing determinant by controlled nonzero factors.
The necessary/sufficient/equivalent conditions to classify are not enumerated; a source-faithful candidate set is required before this can be assessed.
The discrete entry set and admissibility constraints are unspecified, so the number of non-singular matrices cannot be determined safely.
The matrix constraints and allowed entries are not specified; existence/construction depends on those details and must not be invented.
Idempotency is directly checked by A²=A; this is definition-level recognition.
Imposing A²=A on a parameterized matrix creates simultaneous nonlinear entry equations; solving them is a reusable structural-constraint mechanism.
For A²=A, positive powers collapse to A and polynomials reduce using the projection identity, yielding a reusable algebraic-reduction mechanism.
A²=A implies every eigenvalue λ satisfies λ²=λ, so λ∈{0,1}; multiplicities are constrained by rank and nullity. This is a reusable spectral-constraint mechanism.
The polynomial x²−x has distinct roots, so an idempotent matrix is diagonalizable; its similarity class is determined by rank and has canonical form diag(I_r,0).
For idempotents, diagonalizability with eigenvalues 0/1 gives trace=rank, nullity=n−rank and determinant 0 or 1 depending on full rank; this is a multi-invariant deduction mechanism.
I−A is also idempotent, with complementary image/kernel and rank n−rank(A); this is a reusable complement-structure mechanism.

The source groups sums, products, scalar multiples and linear combinations without specifying operand relationships such as commutativity or shared idempotent structure; a safe general rule cannot be inferred.
Idempotency reduces I±αA to scalar actions on the 0/1 eigenspaces, yielding exact invertibility conditions and closed-form inverses; this is a reusable rational-expression mechanism.
The minimal polynomial divides x(x−1) and the characteristic polynomial is x^{n−r}(x−1)^r; linking these polynomials to rank and eigenvalue multiplicity is a distinct algebraic-invariant mechanism.
Existence of nontrivial idempotents under rank/trace/determinant constraints follows from the rank range 1…n−1 and the canonical projection form; this is covered by the rank/similarity archetypes.
Idempotent matrices are similar iff they have the same rank over the stated field; this is already represented by the canonical similarity classification candidate.
The structured classes and property combinations are open-ended; specific families and assumptions must be enumerated before a single archetype can be assessed.
Nilpotency is directly recognized by verifying A^k=O for some positive integer k; the basic definition check is foundation content.
Finding the least positive k with A^k=O requires sequential power analysis and a minimality proof; this is a distinct index-of-nilpotency mechanism.

Parameterized nilpotency imposes simultaneous polynomial constraints on matrix entries; for small orders these can be derived from trace/determinant or powers, forming a reusable constraint mechanism.
All eigenvalues of a nilpotent matrix are zero, so determinant and trace vanish; these are direct consequences.
A nilpotent n×n matrix has characteristic polynomial λ^n and minimal polynomial λ^k for its nilpotency index k; relating these invariants is a distinct polynomial-structure mechanism.
Because N^k=O, any polynomial p(N) reduces to its constant term times I plus a finite sum of lower powers; using the index truncates the expression and is a reusable algebraic-reduction mechanism.
The finite geometric series gives (I−N)⁻¹=I+N+…+N^{k−1} for N^k=O, and the plus-sign variant follows similarly; this is a distinct finite-inverse construction.
Similarity preserves nilpotency and its index by (P⁻¹NP)^k=P⁻¹N^kP; this is a direct invariance property.

Strictly upper/lower triangular matrices are nilpotent, while a triangular matrix with a nonzero diagonal entry cannot be nilpotent; these are standard structural facts already covered by triangular-pattern reasoning.
The nilpotency index is bounded by matrix order and can be sharpened by bandwidth/zero-pattern information; this overlaps the existing nilpotency-bound mechanism.
Nilpotency forces rank(N^k) to decrease until zero, and the index gives a sharp vanishing threshold; relating rank/nullity across powers is a reusable invariant mechanism.
For block triangular matrices, nilpotency is governed by diagonal blocks, while off-diagonal block paths affect the index bound; this is a distinct block-structure mechanism.
Sums/products of nilpotent matrices require specific commutation or compatibility assumptions; the source groups several operations without defining them.
A nilpotent n×n matrix of index k exists exactly for 1≤k≤n; Jordan nilpotent blocks give a constructive existence method.
For nilpotent N, p(N) is invertible exactly when p(0)≠0; factor the constant term and invert the nilpotent remainder by a finite geometric series.
Involutory recognition is a direct check of A²=I.
Imposing A²=I on a parameterized matrix yields simultaneous quadratic entry constraints; solving them is a reusable structural-constraint mechanism.
An involutory matrix is its own inverse because A²=I; this is a direct consequence.
Powers alternate between I and A, so any polynomial reduces to aI+bA according to even/odd coefficient sums; this is a reusable algebraic-reduction mechanism.
A²=I forces eigenvalues to ±1; multiplicities determine trace and determinant and provide a distinct spectral-constraint mechanism.
Trace and determinant follow directly from the multiplicities of eigenvalues ±1 and are already covered by the spectral multiplicity candidate.
An involutory matrix has minimal polynomial dividing (x−1)(x+1) with distinct roots, so it is diagonalizable and similar to diag(I_r,−I_{n−r}); this is a distinct canonical classification mechanism.
The matrices P±=(I±A)/2 are complementary idempotent projectors onto the ±1 eigenspaces; constructing and using these projectors is a reusable decomposition mechanism.
Ranks/nullities of I±A are dimensions of the corresponding eigenspaces and follow from the projector decomposition; this is represented by the projector candidate.
The minimal polynomial divides x²−1 and the characteristic polynomial has only roots ±1; relating polynomial constraints and multiplicities is a distinct invariant mechanism.
For involutory A and B, (AB)²=I exactly when AB=BA; the product condition reduces to commutativity, a distinct reusable mechanism.
Because A²=I, αI+βA has a closed-form inverse proportional to αI−βA when α²−β²≠0; singular exceptional cases follow from the ±1 eigenspaces.
Feasibility depends on the field, order, trace/determinant constraints and whether nontriviality is required; the source does not specify these assumptions.
Permutation-matrix recognition is a direct check of exactly one 1 in each row and column and zeros elsewhere.
Constructing the permutation matrix from a specified permutation is direct representation and indexing.
Recovering the row-to-column mapping from the single 1 in each row is direct permutation decoding.
There are n! permutation matrices of order n, a direct bijection with permutations.
The determinant of a permutation matrix is the sign of its permutation; computing parity from inversions or cycles is a distinct combinatorial-algebraic mechanism.
A permutation matrix is orthogonal, so P⁻¹=Pᵀ; this is a direct property.
Left and right multiplication by permutation matrices reorder rows and columns respectively; tracking the induced index mapping is a distinct transformation mechanism.
Multiplication of permutation matrices corresponds to composition of their permutations; order and composition direction must be tracked carefully.
The order of a permutation matrix is the least common multiple of its disjoint cycle lengths; this is a distinct cycle-decomposition mechanism.
Powers act by advancing positions within each cycle; periodicity and return to identity are determined by cycle lengths and modular arithmetic.
The trace counts fixed points because diagonal entries are 1 exactly at fixed indices; this is a direct read-off property.
P=Pᵀ=P⁻¹ exactly when the permutation is self-inverse, so every cycle has length one or two; this is a distinct structural classification.
Left/right multiplication by a permutation matrix permutes rows/columns and scales determinant by the sign of the permutation; this is a reusable determinant-transformation mechanism.
Conjugation PAP⁻¹ simultaneously relabels rows and columns; determining P for a target relabeling is a distinct index-mapping mechanism.

archetypes.reasoning_path: For row equivalence, express B=EA with E a product of elementary matrices; for column equivalence, express B=AF; derive preserved row/column space and rank conditions; construct or verify a finite operation sequence when required.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine whether two specified elementary matrices commute and establish commutativity conditions
archetypes.archetype: Classify when two elementary matrices commute
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Compare the two operation matrices by type, affected indices and order to derive necessary and sufficient conditions for E₁E₂=E₂E₁.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write both elementary matrices explicitly; compute E₁E₂ and E₂E₁ or compare their actions on a generic matrix; split by swap/scaling/addition types and index overlap; derive exact parameter/index conditions.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine whether a specified single-step matrix transformation can be achieved by one elementary row or column operation and identify the operation when possible
archetypes.archetype: Recognize whether a transformation is a single elementary operation
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Test whether a given transformation matrix matches exactly one elementary-matrix pattern and recover the corresponding operation if it does.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compare with identity; test whether the difference is a single allowed row/column swap, nonzero scaling or one row/column addition; reject matrices requiring multiple changes; identify the unique operation and verify it.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine the combined effect on a matrix of pre- and post-multiplication by specified elementary matrices
archetypes.archetype: Track combined row and column transformations by pre/post multiplication
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Interpret E_L A E_R as a row operation followed by a column operation, preserving the correct left/right order and tracking the combined entry changes.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Apply E_L on the left to transform rows; apply E_R on the right to transform columns; calculate the combined result in the stated order; track affected row/column intersections; verify dimensions and the resulting matrix.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine constraints on entries or parameters required for a matrix to be Hermitian
archetypes.archetype: Derive parameter and missing-entry constraints for a Hermitian matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Translate A*=A into real-diagonal and conjugate-pair constraints on entries, then solve the resulting parameter or missing-entry system.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compare aᵢⱼ with conjugate(aⱼᵢ); require each diagonal entry to be real; impose conjugate-pair conditions for i≠j; solve the coupled real/imaginary parameter equations; verify A*=A.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine conditions under which a product AB is Hermitian given properties of A and B
archetypes.archetype: Determine when a product of Hermitian matrices is Hermitian
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use adjoint reversal (AB)*=B*A* to reduce Hermiticity of a product of Hermitian factors to commutativity and related order conditions.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Apply (AB)*=B*A; compare with AB; derive AB=BA as the necessary and sufficient condition when both factors are Hermitian; extend carefully to multiple factors and verify assumptions.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Infer real-valued scalar invariants such as trace and determinant for a Hermitian matrix
archetypes.archetype: Infer real trace and determinant invariants of a Hermitian matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use the real spectrum of a Hermitian matrix to prove trace and determinant are real and derive further constraints from eigenvalue information.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Apply the spectral theorem or Hermitian eigenvalue property; express trace as the sum and determinant as the product of real eigenvalues; use characteristic-polynomial coefficients when needed; verify any supplied invariant constraints.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine the Hermitian nature of matrices of the form A*A and AA* for arbitrary complex A
archetypes.archetype: Establish positive semidefiniteness of A*A and AA*
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Show that A*A and AA* are Hermitian and that their quadratic forms are nonnegative, linking the matrices to squared vector norms.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute (A*A)*=A*A and (AA*)*=AA*; evaluate x*A*Ax=||Ax||² and x*AA*x=||A*x||²; infer positive semidefiniteness and identify when equality occurs.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine preservation of Hermitian property under congruence transformations P*AP
archetypes.archetype: Prove Hermitian structure is preserved by congruence transformations
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use adjoint reversal to show P*AP remains Hermitian when A is Hermitian, even when P is rectangular and the resulting matrix has compatible square order.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Take the adjoint of P*AP; reverse product order; use A*=A; obtain (P*AP)*=P*AP; verify dimensions and distinguish congruence from similarity.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Characterize Hermitian matrices using the condition that x*Ax is real for all complex vectors x
archetypes.archetype: Characterize Hermitian matrices through real quadratic forms
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Prove that A is Hermitian exactly when x*Ax is real for every complex vector x, using basis vectors and pairwise test vectors to recover entry constraints.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Assume x*Ax is real for all x; choose standard basis vectors to show diagonal entries are real; choose e_i+e_j and e_i+i e_j to derive conjugate-pair relations; conclude A*=A; verify the forward implication directly.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine the number of independent real parameters of n×n Hermitian matrices
archetypes.archetype: Count independent real parameters of a Hermitian matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Count real degrees of freedom by separating real diagonal entries from freely chosen complex entries above the diagonal and their conjugates below.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Count n real diagonal entries; choose one arbitrary complex number (two real parameters) for each of n(n−1)/2 off-diagonal pairs; sum to n+n(n−1)=n²; verify small-order cases.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine conditions or unknown entries for a matrix to be skew-Hermitian
archetypes.archetype: Derive parameter and missing-entry constraints for a skew-Hermitian matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Translate A*=−A into purely imaginary diagonal conditions and negative-conjugate off-diagonal pair constraints, then solve the parameter system.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compare aᵢⱼ with −conjugate(aⱼᵢ); require each diagonal entry to be purely imaginary; impose paired negative-conjugate relations; solve real/imaginary parameter equations; verify A*=−A.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine constraints on the determinant of a skew-Hermitian matrix with respect to matrix order
archetypes.archetype: Infer determinant reality or pure-imaginary character from skew-Hermitian order
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use conjugation of the determinant and A*=−A to derive an order-parity condition on det(A).
archetypes.reasoning_path: Take determinants in A*=−A; use det(A*)=conjugate(det A) and det(−A)=(-1)^n det A; compare the two expressions; conclude det(A) is real for even n and purely imaginary for odd n; verify with low-order examples.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine preservation of the skew-Hermitian property under linear combinations and identify scalar conditions
archetypes.archetype: Classify scalar combinations of skew-Hermitian matrices
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use (cA)*=conjugate(c)A* to determine which scalar coefficients preserve skew-Hermiticity or convert a skew-Hermitian matrix into a Hermitian one.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute (cA)*; substitute A*=−A; compare with cA for skew-Hermiticity and with cA for Hermiticity; solve the scalar conjugation condition; extend to sums of multiple skew-Hermitian matrices.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine the Hermitian or skew-Hermitian nature of powers or polynomials of a skew-Hermitian matrix
archetypes.archetype: Classify powers and polynomials of skew-Hermitian matrices
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use (A^k)*=(−1)^kA^k to classify powers by parity and reduce polynomial expressions into Hermitian/skew-Hermitian components.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Apply adjoint to A^k; reverse factor order (identical factors); simplify the sign by parity; split a polynomial into even and odd powers; apply coefficient conjugation constraints to determine the resulting Hermitian/skew-Hermitian character.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Infer constraints on eigenvalues of a skew-Hermitian matrix
archetypes.archetype: Infer purely imaginary eigenvalues of a skew-Hermitian matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use A*=−A and the eigenvector equation to show every eigenvalue of a skew-Hermitian matrix has zero real part.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Let Av=λv for nonzero v; compute v*Av=λ||v||²; use A*=−A to show conjugate(v*Av)=−v*Av; infer λ+conjugate(λ)=0; conclude λ is purely imaginary.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Infer the nature of the scalar x*Ax when A is skew-Hermitian
archetypes.archetype: Determine the scalar nature of x*Ax for skew-Hermitian A
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use conjugation of the quadratic form and A*=−A to prove x*Ax is purely imaginary (including zero).
archetypes.reasoning_path: Take the complex conjugate of x*Ax; rewrite as x*A*x; substitute A*=−A; obtain conjugate(x*Ax)=−x*Ax; conclude its real part is zero.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Classify AB ± BA as Hermitian or skew-Hermitian given the types of A and B
archetypes.archetype: Classify AB±BA using Hermitian and skew-Hermitian operand types
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Apply adjoint reversal and sign substitution to classify anticommutators and commutators of Hermitian/skew-Hermitian matrices.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute (AB)*=B*A*; substitute A*=±A and B*=±B; reverse factor order; add or subtract the original expression; identify the resulting Hermitian/skew-Hermitian sign and any required commutation conditions.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine parameter conditions for a matrix to be unitary
archetypes.archetype: Derive parameter constraints for a unitary matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Translate U*U=I into simultaneous complex norm and orthogonality equations for columns (or rows), then solve the coupled parameter system.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute U*; form U*U; equate diagonal entries to 1 and off-diagonal entries to 0; separate real and imaginary parts of each complex equation; solve for the parameters; verify all orthonormality constraints and square order.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine scalar conditions under which a scalar multiple of a unitary matrix is unitary
archetypes.archetype: Determine scalar multiples that preserve unitarity
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use (cU)*(cU)=|c|²I to derive the necessary and sufficient unit-modulus condition for a scalar multiple of a unitary matrix.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute (cU)*=conjugate(c)U*; multiply by cU; use U*U=I; obtain |c|²I; conclude |c|=1; verify the converse.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine determinant constraints of unitary matrices
archetypes.archetype: Derive determinant modulus constraints for a unitary matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Take determinants in U*U=I to show the determinant lies on the unit circle and use this to constrain parameterized unitary matrices.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Apply det(U*U)=det(I); use det(U*)=conjugate(det U); obtain |det U|²=1; conclude |det U|=1; combine with any given phase or determinant constraints.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Characterize diagonal unitary matrices
archetypes.archetype: Characterize diagonal unitary matrices entrywise
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Reduce U*U=I for a diagonal matrix to independent modulus-one conditions on each diagonal entry.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write U=diag(u₁,...,uₙ); compute U*=diag(conjugate(u₁),...,conjugate(uₙ)); equate U*U to I; obtain |uᵢ|=1 for every i; construct or classify all admissible entries.
variation_dimensions: roots of unity versus arbitrary unit complex values

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Characterize triangular unitary matrices
archetypes.archetype: Characterize triangular unitary matrices as diagonal phase matrices
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use triangularity and column orthonormality to show all off-diagonal entries vanish, leaving diagonal entries of modulus one.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Use U*U=I; apply unit norm to each column and orthogonality between distinct columns; combine with upper/lower triangular zero pattern to force off-diagonal entries to zero; conclude U is diagonal with |uᵢᵢ|=1; verify the converse.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine unitarity of block-diagonal matrices from the unitarity of their blocks
archetypes.archetype: Determine unitarity of block-diagonal matrices from their blocks
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Reduce U*U=I for a block-diagonal matrix to independent unitary conditions on each diagonal block.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Write U=diag(U₁,...,Uₖ); compute U*=diag(U₁*,...,Uₖ*); multiply blockwise; equate each block Uᵢ*Uᵢ with its identity; verify compatible block sizes and converse.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Establish norm-preservation by unitary matrices for vectors
archetypes.archetype: Use unitary transformations to preserve complex inner products and norms
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Apply U*U=I to show (Ux)*(Uy)=x*y and hence ||Ux||=||x||, then transfer vector constraints through the transformation.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Compute (Ux)*(Uy)=x*U*Uy=x*y; set x=y to obtain norm preservation; use the identity to preserve angles/orthogonality; apply to the specified vectors or unknown transform.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine admissible block partitions for a given square matrix size
archetypes.archetype: Determine admissible block partitions of a fixed matrix order
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Translate a square matrix order and block-size restrictions into positive-integer partition constraints, then enumerate or count the admissible block structures.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Let the total order be n; express it as a sum of positive block sizes; apply minimum/maximum/equality restrictions; solve the integer partition conditions; distinguish ordered block sizes from unordered partitions according to the stated partition convention.

archetypes.subject: Mathematics
archetypes.question_possibility: Determine the determinant of a block diagonal matrix from determinants of its blocks
archetypes.archetype: Factor determinant and singularity conditions of a block-diagonal matrix
archetypes.assessment_mechanism: Use det(diag(A₁,...,Aₖ))=∏det(Aᵢ) to reduce determinant, invertibility and singularity questions to the diagonal blocks.
archetypes.reasoning_path: Identify the diagonal blocks; apply the determinant product formula; determine when the total determinant is zero/nonzero; isolate parameter conditions blockwise; verify compatible square block sizes and the converse.
variation_dimensions: singularity of one versus multiple blocks
